edges.description: Notch receptors are among the ADAM10 substrates in the skin, so reduced ADAM10 activity is proposed to reduce Notch ectodomain cleavage.
edges.target: Impaired Notch Receptor Processing in Epidermis

edges.description: Loss of ADAM10 removes a restraint on melanocyte expansion in adult skin.
Disturbed Notch signaling is proposed to alter the maintenance of epidermal melanocytes. The direct step from Notch processing to melanocyte number has not been shown in this disorder.
edges.source: Impaired Notch Receptor Processing in Epidermis

edges.description: Local melanocyte expansion and increased basal melanin produce the reticulate acral macules.
A dominant Adam10 loss-of-function allele produces freckle-like macules made of clusters of epidermal melanocytes.
edges.limitations: The macules form only on a Hairless (Hr/Hr) homozygous background, which itself causes epidermal pigmentation in aging mice, and the model was not reported to show acral distribution or palmoplantar pits.

edges.description: Complete epidermal loss of Adam10 strongly reduces Notch processing and Notch signaling.
edges.limitations: The deletion is homozygous, whereas patients carry one defective ADAM10 copy, and the mice die perinatally with barrier failure and absent sebaceous glands. No pigmentary phenotype resembling the human acral reticulate hyperpigmentation was reported.
edges.target: Impaired Notch Receptor Processing in Epidermis

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADAM10 mutations as a cause of reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura, a clinical entity distinct from Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: We identified a total of three truncating mutations, a splice site mutation and a missense mutation in ADAM10.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADAM10 mutations as a cause of reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura, a clinical entity distinct from Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: These results reveal that mutations in ADAM10 are a cause of RAK and that RAK is an independent clinical entity distinct from DDD.

nodes.description: Heterozygous truncating, splice-site and missense ADAM10 variants reduce ADAM10 metalloprotease activity in the skin. ADAM10 carries out the ectodomain shedding of many membrane proteins in the epidermis.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADAM10 mutations as a cause of reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura, a clinical entity distinct from Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: ADAM10 is known to be involved in the ectodomain shedding of various substrates in the skin.

evidence.reference_title: Adam10 haploinsufficiency causes freckle-like macules in Hairless mice.
evidence.snippet: Through linkage analysis, we find that the Pied mutation is a 1914 base pair loss-of-function deletion in the Adam10 zinc metalloprotease gene.

nodes.description: Hyperpigmented lesions contain more basal melanocytes than perilesional skin, and more melanosomes are transferred into keratinocytes. In the Adam10 mouse model, macules are local clusters of epidermal melanocytes.

animal_models.description: A dominant Adam10 loss-of-function allele produces freckle-like macules made of clusters of epidermal melanocytes.
animal_models.genotype: Adam10 heterozygous 1914-bp loss-of-function deletion (Pied) on a Hairless (Hr/Hr) background
animal_models.name: Pied (Adam10 loss-of-function) Hairless mouse

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Review of Hereditary Acral Reticulate Pigmentary Disorders.
evidence.snippet: examination of the hyperpigmented areas under electron microscopy shows a significant number of melanocytes in the basal layer and melanosomes in the keratinocyte cytoplasm

evidence.reference_title: Behavior of melanocytes in reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura.
evidence.snippet: It is concluded that the hyperpigmentation of RAPK is due to increased number of active melanocytes and to increased transfer of melanosomes to surrounding keratinocytes.

evidence.reference_title: Adam10 haploinsufficiency causes freckle-like macules in Hairless mice.
evidence.snippet: The Pied macules require Hairless(Hr) homozygosity to form and are composed of localized clusters of epidermal melanocytes.

nodes.description: Reduced ADAM10-mediated cleavage of Notch receptors is the proposed link between ADAM10 variants and the pigmentary phenotype. Epidermal deletion of Adam10 in mice strongly reduces Notch processing and Notch signaling, but the defect has not been measured in patient skin, where only one ADAM10 copy is affected. It would connect this disorder to Dowling-Degos disease, whose POFUT1, POGLUT1 and PSENEN forms also act on Notch processing.
nodes.id: Impaired Notch Receptor Processing in Epidermis

animal_models.description: Complete epidermal loss of Adam10 strongly reduces Notch processing and Notch signaling.
animal_models.genotype: Adam10 homozygous conditional deletion in epidermis (K14-Cre)
animal_models.name: Epidermal Adam10 knockout mouse (K14-Cre)

evidence.reference_title: Dyschromatosis symmetrica hereditaria and reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura: An update.
evidence.snippet: We speculate that the pathogenesis of RAK and Dowling-Degos disease (DDD, a pigmentary disease similar to RAK) is associated with the Notch signaling pathway.

evidence.reference_title: The disintegrin/metalloproteinase Adam10 is essential for epidermal integrity and Notch-mediated signaling.
evidence.snippet: Notch processing is indeed strongly reduced resulting in decreased levels of Notch intracellular domain fragment and functional Notch signaling.

nodes.description: Angulated, punctate, slightly depressed hyperpigmented macules in a reticulate pattern on the dorsa of the hands and feet. They appear before puberty, spread to the proximal limbs and trunk, and darken with time and sun exposure. There are no hypopigmented macules.

evidence.reference_title: Whole-exome sequencing identifies ADAM10 mutations as a cause of reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura, a clinical entity distinct from Dowling-Degos disease.
evidence.snippet: The characteristic skin lesions are reticulate, slightly depressed pigmented macules mainly affecting the dorsa of the hands and feet, which first appear before puberty and subsequently expand to the proximal limb and the trunk.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical and Genetic Review of Hereditary Acral Reticulate Pigmentary Disorders.
evidence.snippet: The typical skin morphology of RAPK includes angulated, punctate, and slightly depressed hyperpigmented macules in a reticulated pattern with no areas of hypopigmentation

evidence.reference_title: Dowling-Degos disease with reticulate acropigmentation of Kitamura: Extended spectrum of a single entity.
evidence.snippet: The macules darken with time and continued sun exposure.
